Unit count: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.

Listing copy names the building "Fifty-Five 55 Dunbar"; listings record year built 2015, Apartment/Condo, frame-wood construction, 4 storeys, and strata plan EPS3033. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED — one directory page titles it a "33 Unit Development" while another directory page for the same address describes it as one of 17 units built after redevelopment; the conflict is flagged, not resolved. A current listing's pet field shows cats OK; full published rental/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.

A four-storey concrete mixed-use building at Dunbar Street and West 39th Avenue: a retail brochure for the site (Plan EPP93856) records 15 residential units above four retail strata units, concrete construction. Current listings record year built 2024, Apartment/Condo, concrete construction, pets allowed (one unit's listing field says "Pets: No" — the conflict is flagged; read the bylaws), and sale by receivership with a disclosure statement, prices including GST and a 2-5-10 new-home warranty — i.e., these are new-build sales, not resales.
Streets, schools and getting around Dunbar

items.t: Dunbar is the residential core of the City of Vancouver's Dunbar-Southlands local area (one of the City's 22), in the city's southwest, north of the Fraser River and east of UBC and Pacific Spirit Regional Park; the City publishes no street-by-street written boundary in the sources read, so exact board boundary roads are UNVERIFIED.

Where condo stock actually concentrates: Dunbar is overwhelmingly detached houses. Its verified strata apartment stock is three low-rise buildings, all on the area's two commercial frontages — Dunbar Street itself (West Pointe at the south end, Fifty-Five 55 Dunbar mid-village) and the Dunbar / West 39th Avenue corner (3590 West 39th Avenue). The interior streets and the Southlands country lots at the south edge have no verified apartment-condo stock.

Retail corridor: the Dunbar Village shopping area on Dunbar Street is the local retail strip; Dunbar Street is the north–south spine, crossed by West 16th Avenue, West King Edward Avenue, West 33rd Avenue and West 41st Avenue, with SW Marine Drive along the south edge.
Transit: no SkyTrain station sits inside Dunbar; route 7 runs the Dunbar Street corridor, with the 2, 25 and 33 on the east–west avenues and the 49 on West 49th Avenue at the south edge.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Dunbar

items.t: Area plan: Dunbar has no separate adopted community plan confirmed in the sources read: UNVERIFIED; citywide direction comes from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026.

City tax timing: Vancouver 2026 advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after each due date; the home owner grant was also due July 3, 2026.

Dunbar's newest condo building is selling out of a receivership. Current listings for 3590 West 39th Avenue state "this is a receivership sale" with a disclosure statement and GST included — a buyer expecting an ordinary strata resale will misread the entire transaction.

Two addresses, one corner, possibly one project. Presale coverage names "Dunbar at 39th" at 3636 West 39th Avenue with 29 condominiums (Wesgroup), while the built building sells from 3590 West 39th Avenue with 15 residential units in its retail brochure. Whether these are the same project is UNCONFIRMED — verify against the disclosure statement before citing either number.

"Dunbar" the condo label can mean a different West Pointe. A separate building also called West Pointe exists at 3250 West Broadway in Kitsilano (built 1990 in directory data) — same name, different building and neighbourhood. Building searches and strata documents must be matched by address, not name.

The whole Dunbar condo market is two streets. All three verified apartment buildings sit on Dunbar Street or at its West 39th Avenue corner — there is no verified strata stock on the interior residential streets at all.

Fifty-Five 55 Dunbar's unit count is genuinely unsettled in public sources. The same directory publishes both 33 units and 17 units for 5555 Dunbar Street — a reminder that directory unit counts are leads, not facts, until the strata plan is read.

Southlands is inside the same City area name but is a different product entirely. Dunbar-Southlands pairs the Dunbar house streets with in-city country lots beside the Musqueam First Nation land, in an area the City notes was inhabited by Indigenous peoples as early as 400 B.C. — a Southlands address is not a Dunbar Village address, and neither prices like the other.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Dunbar

items.t: "Dunbar" is the board / site name for the Dunbar sub-area in Vancouver West (GVR board area); the City of Vancouver's corresponding local area is "Dunbar-Southlands" — one of the City's 22 distinct areas — pairing the Dunbar house streets with the Southlands country lots and the Musqueam First Nation land at its south edge, in the city's southwest, north of the Fraser River and east of UBC and Pacific Spirit Regional Park. The board sub-area and the City local area cover closely related but not identical ground, and the City publishes no street-by-street written boundary in the sources read — exact board boundary roads: UNVERIFIED.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: almost nowhere. Dunbar is overwhelmingly detached houses on tree-lined streets, with the unique urban-country Southlands lots at the south edge.

Retail and roads: the Dunbar Village shopping area on Dunbar Street is the local retail strip; Dunbar Street is the north–south spine, crossed by West 16th Avenue, West King Edward Avenue, West 33rd Avenue and West 41st Avenue, with SW Marine Drive along the south edge by the Fraser River.

Transit: no SkyTrain station sits inside Dunbar; route 7 (Nanaimo Station / Dunbar) runs the Dunbar Street corridor, with cross-corridor routes including the 2, 25 and 33 on the east–west avenues and the 49 on West 49th Avenue at the south edge.

Schools: SD39 catchments are address-based and checked in the VSB School Locator; SD39 has no middle-school tier — elementary is Kindergarten to Grade 7 and secondary is Grades 8 to 12. Schools located in Dunbar-Southlands on the VSB list: Kitchener Elementary, 3455 West King Edward Avenue; Queen Elizabeth Elementary, 4102 West 16th Avenue; and Southlands Elementary, 5351 Camosun Street; the VSB list also places Kerrisdale Elementary, 5555 Carnarvon Street, under the Dunbar-Southlands heading.

Market figures: Vancouver is outside SnapStats coverage in Jared's reports — the SnapStats FVR and GVR September 2026 reports contain no Vancouver community or sub-area rows — so no inventory, solds, sales-ratio, median-price, $/sqft, sale-to-list or days-on-market figure is published here for Dunbar. All market figures for this area: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Dunbar

items.t: Form B diligence (the 3349 Dunbar Street strata, and any Dunbar strata purchase): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.

Fee-simple product (Southlands lots, multiplexes, houses with suites/laneway): NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees — diligence is title, municipal rules (Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575) and any registered covenants only, stated plainly. A Dunbar "townhouse-style" listing with no strata fees charged is usually this form or a duplex, not a strata lot.

SSMUH / suite rules as the city states them: Vancouver's small-scale multi-unit housing is the R1-1 multiplex regime above — up to 6 strata units or up to 8 secured rental units on a qualifying lot, with a secondary suite and a laneway house permitted with a single detached house. That regime prices the house lots around any townhouse purchase; it does not change the strata complexes themselves.

Flood / ALR: the City's designated floodplain covers the Fraser River coastal floodplain at the area's south end, and land in the floodplain is subject to the Vancouver Building By-law Floodplain Standards and Requirements for setbacks and flood construction levels; Southlands lots near the river include land in the Agricultural Land Reserve. Parcel-level status: UNVERIFIED — check the City dataset.
Dunbar's townhouse supply is one documented address, not a market segment. A buyer waiting for "the Dunbar townhouse complexes" to list is waiting on a category that barely exists.

The area's one seniors-specific project is an approval, not a residence. The Amica seniors' community care facility approved for West 41st Avenue at Blenheim Street (232 units in the proposal reported by the Dunbar Residents' Association) has no operator page, opening date or leasing information in the sources checked — its construction and opening status is UNCONFIRMED, and it must not be listed as available seniors housing.

The bus is the transit story, stated plainly. There is no SkyTrain in Dunbar and none planned in the sources read — the pitch is the route 7 Dunbar corridor, the east–west routes to UBC and downtown, and the Pacific Spirit Park edge. A townhouse listing implying rapid-transit access here is marketing ahead of the map.

Established-street house lots: detached houses on tree-lined streets dominate — the City calls Dunbar-Southlands a mature community of quiet residential streets lined with grand old trees — with low-rise strata product concentrated on the Dunbar Street and West 41st Avenue frontages. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees. The strata-versus-freehold split by street: UNVERIFIED.

Lot character, as the research states it: the house streets sit under the R1-1 District Schedule of Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 — minimum site area 306 m² for a single detached house or duplex and for a multiple dwelling of 3 to 4 units (minimum frontage 10.0 m), 464 m² for 5 units (13.4 m), 557 m² for 6 to 8 units (15.1 m); a single detached house may include a secondary suite and a laneway house, and a multiplex may have up to 6 units or up to 8 rental units. These are schedule minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size; parcel-level zone: UNVERIFIED.
Serviced position: Dunbar homes are on City water and sewer services; a 2026 utility dollar figure confirmed on a City source: UNVERIFIED.
Historic subdivisions = built lot fabric, not offerings

Southlands — south edge of Dunbar-Southlands, beside the Musqueam First Nation land: Large, semi-rural freehold properties — the City describes Southlands as a unique urban-country neighbourhood inside Dunbar-Southlands — under their own agricultural / limited-agriculture districts. The exact schedule for a given Southlands parcel: UNVERIFIED. Southlands lots near the river include land in the Agricultural Land Reserve; parcel-level ALR status: UNVERIFIED — check ALC mapping parcel by parcel before applying any ALR rule. This is in-city country-lot stock with houses on it, not a bare-land subdivision and not lots for sale as a program.

ALR vs non-ALR split: no percentage split is stated — ALR status is confirmed only in the research as present on lots near the river at the south edge, parcel by parcel UNVERIFIED. Flood position: the area's south edge slopes to the Fraser River and the City's designated floodplain covers the Fraser River coastal floodplain at the south end of the city; parcels in it carry Vancouver Building By-law setback and flood construction level requirements. Parcel-level flood status: UNVERIFIED.

No bare-land strata plan or community in Dunbar was verified: Stated plainly: a bare-land strata lot, wherever it exists in BC, IS strata tenure (Form B / strata fees / bylaws apply —); no such plan is documented for this ground.

3590 West 39th Avenue (Dunbar at West 39th) — built strata development, selling by receivership: A four-storey concrete mixed-use building at Dunbar Street and West 39th Avenue: a retail brochure for the site (Plan EPP93856) records 15 residential units above four retail strata units; current listings record year built 2024 and sale by receivership with a disclosure statement, prices including GST and a 2-5-10 new-home warranty — new-build sales, not resales, and not lots.
Built strata frontage stock — cross-reference only

Amica seniors' project — 3329–3429 West 41st Avenue / 5649–5683 Blenheim Street: It is a rezoning approval on assembled ground — care/rental product in any case, never a lot offering and never inventory.
No other specific Dunbar project: was verified on a City development-application page in the research: UNVERIFIED.
: The West 39th Avenue activity above sold strata units, not lots, and no presale lot program was verified on a developer or government source.

Roads and retail: Dunbar Street is the north–south spine, crossed by West 16th Avenue, West King Edward Avenue, West 33rd Avenue and West 41st Avenue, with SW Marine Drive along the south edge by the Fraser River. The Dunbar Village shopping area on Dunbar Street is the local retail strip.

Transit: no SkyTrain station sits inside Dunbar. Route 7 (Nanaimo Station / Dunbar) runs the Dunbar Street corridor, with the 2, 25 and 33 on the east–west avenues and the 49 on West 49th Avenue at the south edge. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Civic anchors: Dunbar Community Centre is the area's Park Board community centre, with a fitness centre; its civic address was not captured on the City page read: UNVERIFIED. The Dunbar Branch library's civic address was not confirmed on a VPL page: UNVERIFIED. The City names McCleery Golf Course as a local feature, and Pacific Spirit Regional Park borders the area to the west. Nearest hospital confirmed on a health-authority page: UNVERIFIED.

Schools: SD39 catchments are address-based, with no middle-school tier (K–7 / 8–12). Schools located in Dunbar-Southlands on the VSB list: Kitchener Elementary, 3455 West King Edward Avenue; Queen Elizabeth Elementary, 4102 West 16th Avenue; and Southlands Elementary, 5351 Camosun Street; the VSB list also places Kerrisdale Elementary, 5555 Carnarvon Street, under the Dunbar-Southlands heading. Secondary school name and address confirmed on an official source for Dunbar in the research pass: UNVERIFIED. School names use Ministry-listed names only.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Dunbar

items.t: Plan — no separate Dunbar plan + Vancouver Official Development Plan: Dunbar has no separate adopted community plan confirmed in the sources read: UNVERIFIED; citywide direction comes from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026.

Subdivision — Subdivision By-law No. 5208, fees by No. 14538: Vancouver subdivision is governed by the Subdivision By-law (No. 5208), whose Schedule A sets minimum parcel width and area standards by district and sub-area category, administered by the Approving Officer; its fee schedule was most recently amended for 2026 by By-law No. 14538 (enacted December 9, 2025, in force January 1, 2026). A fee-simple split of a Dunbar house lot must clear both R1-1 and its Subdivision By-law category; a Southlands split additionally clears its own district — and, where the parcel is in the ALR, ALC approval (below).

ALR rules (live for Southlands parcels in the ALR; parcel status UNVERIFIED until checked): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

Strata diligence (the frontage strata stock — and any bare-land strata lot, if one is ever met here): No Dunbar building is published as 55+ — Fifty-Five 55 Dunbar's "55" is its street number, not an age bylaw.

Dunbar's newest building is selling out of a receivership: current listings for 3590 West 39th Avenue state "this is a receivership sale" with a disclosure statement and GST included — a buyer expecting an ordinary strata resale will misread the entire transaction.

Two addresses, one corner, possibly one project: presale coverage names "Dunbar at 39th" at 3636 West 39th Avenue with 29 condominiums (Wesgroup), while the built building sells from 3590 West 39th Avenue with 15 residential units in its retail brochure. Whether these are the same project is UNCONFIRMED — verify against the disclosure statement before citing either number.

"Dunbar" the condo label can mean a different West Pointe: a separate building also called West Pointe exists at 3250 West Broadway in Kitsilano (built 1990 in directory data) — same name, different building and neighbourhood. Dunbar's West Pointe is 5629 Dunbar Street. Match documents by address, not name.

Page-statement check for this area. Approved page claims, where a live page states them, are the settled set only: REALTOR since 2015; 10 straight years in the FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points for 2025 and 2026 YTD; more than $500M in sales.

faq.q: Is Dunbar an official City of Vancouver area?
faq.a: The City's local area is "Dunbar-Southlands," one of its 22 distinct areas, pairing the Dunbar house streets with Southlands and the Musqueam land at the south edge; "Dunbar" is the board / site name for the residential core.

faq.q: Which schools are located in Dunbar-Southlands?
faq.a: On the VSB list: Kitchener Elementary (3455 West King Edward Avenue), Queen Elizabeth Elementary (4102 West 16th Avenue) and Southlands Elementary (5351 Camosun Street), with Kerrisdale Elementary (5555 Carnarvon Street) also listed under the Dunbar-Southlands heading; catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the VSB locator.

faq.q: Is there a SkyTrain station in Dunbar?
faq.a: No — Dunbar is bus-served, with route 7 running the Dunbar Street corridor between Nanaimo Station and the Dunbar loop, and east-west routes serving UBC and downtown.

faq.q: What makes Southlands different from the rest of Dunbar?
faq.a: The City describes Southlands as a unique urban-country neighbourhood inside Dunbar-Southlands, beside the Musqueam First Nation land, in an area inhabited by Indigenous peoples as early as 400 B.C. and farmed since the 1800s.

faq.q: How much condo choice is there in Dunbar, really?
faq.a: Three verified apartment buildings: West Pointe (2000) and Fifty-Five 55 Dunbar (2015) on Dunbar Street, and the new concrete building at 3590 West 39th Avenue (2024). Everything else in the area is houses, the 3349 Dunbar Street townhouses, or Southlands country lots.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Dunbar condo long-term?
faq.a: Yes — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, so West Pointe's "Rentals Allwd w/Restrctns" listing field cannot stop a long-term tenancy. Short-term rentals can still be restricted, and the Empty Homes Tax declaration applies to a unit left empty.

faq.q: Why do listings at 3590 West 39th Avenue say "price includes GST" and "receivership sale"?
faq.a: Because those units are selling as new construction through a receivership, with a disclosure statement and 2-5-10 warranty — the buyer is purchasing from the developer side, not from a homeowner. That changes the paperwork (REDMA disclosure instead of a Form B), the tax (5% GST, partly offset by the Newly Built Home Exemption and the Bill C-4 rebate where the buyer qualifies), and the diligence (confirm the receiver's authority and warranty enrolment).

faq.q: How many units are in Fifty-Five 55 Dunbar?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED — directory sources conflict (33 units on one page, 17 units on another for the same address and strata plan EPS3033). The Form B and the strata plan itself settle it; do not rely on either directory figure.

faq.q: What should I check in West Pointe, the oldest of the three?
faq.a: The depreciation report: stratas with 5+ lots must have one every five years (no deferral vote since July 1, 2024) and must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF. In a 2000 building, envelope, roof and elevator items in the report matter more than the unit's finish.

faq.q: Is there actually a townhouse complex I can buy in Dunbar?
faq.a: The one documented townhouse address is 3349 Dunbar Street — an unnamed strata (strata fees charged in the listing record), built 1995, with a current listing describing a 2-level, 3-bedroom home with a 624 sq ft rooftop deck and pets "Yes With Restrictions." Everything else verified in Dunbar is detached houses, three apartment-condo buildings, or Southlands country lots.

faq.q: Strata or fee-simple — how do I tell which Dunbar product I'm looking at?
faq.a: By the strata-fee record and title, not the marketing word "townhome." The 3349 Dunbar Street listing charges strata fees, so it is read as strata here; a Dunbar multiplex, duplex or house-with-laneway showing no strata fees is fee-simple — NO strata, NO Form B, diligence is title and City rules only.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Dunbar townhouse long-term?
faq.a: Yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022, whatever older bylaw text says. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw — read the registered bylaws in the Form B package — and a unit left empty instead triggers the Vancouver Empty Homes Tax declaration at 3%.
